title: Agent sets ExternalPart.expires from the server's blob lifetime
description: Follow-up of mimid-1wgh.14.2 (decision mimid-1wgh.67). mimid-server deletes every blob blob_lifetime_secs (30 days by default) after upload, but mimid-agent-core's Sealed::part sets ExternalPart.expires = 0 (mimi-content-10 §4.5: never). The server would need to advertise its lifetime (no JMAP or JMAP Chat MIMI field exists: INVENTED, NOT FROM SPEC unless draft-atwood-jmap-chat-mimi gains one), or the upload response carry an expiry; then the agent sets expires to upload time plus lifetime, and the receiver already refuses expired parts (agent.rs fetch). Needs a decision on the field.
notes:
Mark 2026-11-19: spec field. jmap-chat-spec 120db2c adds account-level assetLifetime (UnsignedInt, optional, seconds after upload a blob stays at assetUrl); client MAY set ExternalPart.expires = upload time + assetLifetime. mimid: server advertises blob_lifetime_secs as assetLifetime (typed field once crate-jmap has it, asked of the crate-jmap session); agent sets Sealed part expires from it.
crate-jmap 56ac33f1 (JMAP-it7g.8): MimiCapability.asset_lifetime Option<u64>, serde assetLifetime. Do after mimid-cu6d (that bump pins >= 56ac33f1).
close_reason: Done in 4ce0d5d (branch asset-lifetime): server advertises assetLifetime = blob_lifetime_secs; agent sets ExternalPart.expires = upload time (sender clock, upload response has none) + assetLifetime, saturated to u32; absent -> 0.
